title: Ssam Lettuce and Herb Platter
shortDescription: A crisp, carefully washed assortment of leaf lettuce, perilla, cucumber, mild chile, garlic, and optional crown daisy for wrapping grilled food with rice and ssamjang.
culturalContext: Ssam refers to wrapping a bite of food in edible leaves, and Korean tables may offer many cultivated and seasonal greens. This practical platter is a flexible selection rather than a fixed canonical list; ingredient names and availability require Korean editorial review.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Chef’s knife and dedicated produce cutting board

instructions.heading: Inspect the produce
instructions.action: Discard wilted, slimy, bruised, or decayed leaves and trim damaged portions from otherwise sound vegetables.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Selected leaves are crisp, brightly colored, and free of slime or off odor.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep ready-to-eat produce separate from raw meat, poultry, and seafood from shopping through service.

instructions.heading: Wash the greens
instructions.action: Wash hands, clean the basin, then rinse lettuce, perilla, and crown daisy under cool running water, gently separating folds where grit collects.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: No visible grit remains and the final rinse water is clear.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not use soap, bleach, or detergent on produce; use potable running water and a clean basin.

instructions.heading: Dry thoroughly
instructions.action: Spin greens in small batches or blot with clean towels. Refrigerate 15 minutes in a clean container lined with a dry towel.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Leaves are dry enough that water does not pool on the platter.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a cleaned salad spinner and fresh towels to avoid recontaminating washed leaves.

instructions.heading: Prepare the garnishes
instructions.action: Wash cucumber and chiles under running water, dry them, and cut on a clean produce-only board. Slice garlic with a clean knife.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Cucumber batons and chile rings are even and easy to tuck into a wrap.
instructions.safetyNote: Avoid touching eyes after cutting chiles and wash hands and tools afterward.

instructions.heading: Arrange the platter
instructions.action: Fan sturdy lettuce around the platter, stack perilla in small bundles, and place delicate herbs, cucumber, chiles, and garlic in separate groups.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Leaves are easy to lift one at a time and wet ingredients do not sit on top of them.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a clean chilled platter and clean serving tongs.

instructions.heading: Serve cold
instructions.action: Serve alongside hot cooked food, rice, and a separately spooned sauce. Replenish with small chilled batches rather than overfilling the table platter.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Leaves remain crisp and cool throughout service.
instructions.safetyNote: Discard platter portions contaminated by raw meat utensils or left unrefrigerated for more than 2 hours.

grillSetup: No grill is used for the platter; keep it physically separated from the raw-meat side of any tabletop grilling station.
visualDonenessCues: Leaves are crisp, dry, and free of grit
No slimy or decayed produce remains
Platter stays chilled and visually separate from raw-meat tools
foodSafetyNotes: Wash hands and sanitize the sink, basin, spinner, board, and platter before handling ready-to-eat greens.
Rinse produce under cool potable running water without soap or bleach.
Keep washed produce separate from raw animal foods and their utensils.
Refrigerate prepared greens at or below 40°F / 4°C until service.
Discard contaminated or temperature-abused platter portions rather than returning them to storage.

allergens.crossContactWarning: The platter itself contains none of the listed major allergens, but sauces and grilled foods served beside it commonly contain soy, wheat, sesame, fish, or shellfish; use separate tongs and bowls.

substitutions: Use butter lettuce or romaine hearts when Korean leaf lettuce is unavailable.
Omit perilla or crown daisy if unavailable rather than substituting unrelated strongly flavored herbs without testing.
ingredientSourcing: Choose unwilted lettuce and perilla with crisp stems and no slimy edges.
Korean markets may label mixed wrapping greens as ssam chaeso; confirm each unfamiliar plant is intended for raw culinary use.
makeAhead: Wash and dry sturdy greens up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate between clean towels; cut cucumber, chile, and garlic within 2 hours of service.
storage: Refrigerate dry greens in a clean sealed container and use within 2 days; discard any portion exposed to raw-food utensils or extended room-temperature service.
leftovers: Use only uncontaminated, continuously chilled leftovers in a salad the next day; discard table-exposed leaves if their handling is uncertain.
servingSuggestions: Layer rice, a small piece of grilled food, and ssamjang in one leaf
Use perilla inside lettuce for a two-leaf wrap

faq.question: What makes a good ssam leaf?
faq.answer: It should be fresh, flexible enough to fold, and large enough to hold one compact bite without tearing.

faq.question: Can I wash greens with soap?
faq.answer: No. Rinse produce under cool potable running water and rely on clean hands, tools, and separation from raw foods.
